real.title: Expose command line interface
real.excerpt: Date: 2018-09-02 ## Status Accepted ## Context We want to maximise the usability of adr-viewer whilst maintaining flexibility in future for other output formats, e.g. a live webserver. ## Decision The entry point for this project will be a command-line utility called `adr-viewer`. We will use the python [click](http://click.pocoo.org/5/) library to provide command-line options and documentation. ## Consequences Click will be added as a dependency, and further improvements should consider the user experience of the command-line interface.

reconstructed.title: Adopt click for CLI interface
reconstructed.context: The project needed a command‑line interface to generate HTML from ADR files. The developers wanted sensible defaults for the ADR directory and output file, and automatic help text. The existing code did not have a CLI framework, and the repository’s requirements were empty before this change.
reconstructed.decision: Add the `click` library as a dependency and refactor the entry point to use click’s command and option decorators.
reconstructed.consequences: The `requirements.txt` and `setup.py` now list `click` as a required package. The `main` function is now a click command with `--adr-path` and `--output` options, and the help output shows default values (as later documented). Future code that invokes the CLI will rely on click, tying the project to that library. No other CLI framework appears in the history, so click becomes the de‑facto standard for this project.
reconstructed.inference: The decision appears to be driven by the need for a lightweight, declarative CLI that provides built‑in help and default handling, which `click` offers. The commit message explicitly mentions using click for the CLI, and the subsequent docs commit leverages click’s help output, suggesting the developers chose click to simplify CLI development and improve user experience.

real.title: Loader Multi-Worker Pipeline
real.excerpt: ## Status Accepted ## Context The Plex loader previously executed ingestion, enrichment, and Qdrant writes sequentially. Each phase waited for the previous phase to finish, so TMDb and IMDb lookups, embedding generation, and upsert requests could not overlap. Large libraries therefore spent most of their time idle while waiting on network latency, and any failure in a downstream phase required rerunning the entire load. Stakeholders asked for the "loader multi worker rearchitecture plan" to overlap these phases, provide better fault isolation, and expose concurrency controls. reconstructed.title: Adopt coverage for test measurement
reconstructed.context: The project needed a way to measure test coverage for its Python code base. Existing test suites were expanding, and developers wanted a standard tool to enforce coverage thresholds. The repository uses pyproject.toml to declare development dependencies, so adding a new dev‑dependency would be the natural integration point.
reconstructed.decision: The team added the `coverage[toml]` package to the development dependencies in both the root and Docker manifests.
reconstructed.consequences: All subsequent commits continue to list `coverage[toml]` in the dependency manifests, indicating the dependency is now part of the baseline environment. Test files were expanded with additional imports (e.g., `io`, `sys`, `datetime`) that are typical for coverage‑related fixtures, suggesting the new tool is being exercised. The version bump to 1.0.0 later in the history reflects a stable release that now includes coverage support. A trade‑off is the added dependency size and the need for developers to run coverage commands as part of the CI pipeline.
reconstructed.inference: The decision to adopt coverage appears to be driven by a desire for measurable test quality as the code base grew. The commit message explicitly mentions adding coverage‑focused tests, and the manifest change introduces the package as a dev dependency, which is the standard way to integrate such tooling in Python projects. Subsequent commits retain the dependency, implying the team accepted the change and incorporated it into the CI workflow.
